Proposal question: RQ2 (H2 of the proposal): how much of the spike do upwind fires explain after controlling for weather; does fire radiative power add explanatory power?
Notebook hypothesis and cells: Notebook H1, 8B.6 and the fire-radiative-power run of 8.7
Result: H1 WEAKLY SUPPORTED (frozen rule met); fire counts add 1.8 points of R-squared beyond weather and stations (interval 0.01 to 7.21); fire radiative power: +8.8% per SD (interval +1.5% to +16.5%)

Proposal question: RQ3 (H3 of the proposal): does weather explain most of the variation; are boundary-layer height and wind speed among the top predictors?
Notebook hypothesis and cells: 8B.6, 8B.9 (permutation importance of the boosted model) and 9A (the ventilation index, H3)
Result: stations and weather explain 45% of log PM2.5; shuffling the weather inputs raises the test error by 28.9 ug/m3; boundary-layer height ranks 9 and wind speed 4 of 11 inputs; the ventilation index of 8C goes with -19.1% PM2.5 per +1 SD (interval -22.8% to -15.3%), supported
Status: not supported by this measure (top 3 taken as 'among the top')
Gap: not a frozen rule; temperature, pressure and boundary-layer height move together, so single-input ranks (some even negative) are unstable, while the weather inputs shuffled together matter most
